title: Ops stitch: week-of Dec 13-20, 2026 — handoff & stability notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
Quick stitching doc to capture the run of week ops events, outstanding SLO pressure items, and explicit on-call handoff notes. Intended as a concise augmentation to the formal RCA drafts (linked) and the SLO dashboard snapshots. Use this during handoffs and for the Tuesday SRE sync.

TL;DR (one-liners):
- P99 embeddings latency spike on Dec 17 (35m) due to KV cache invalidation cascade; partial mitigation via emergency cache-warm job; continuing follow-up. (INC-2026-1187)
- Autoscaler thrash observed on Dec 15 evening for dedicated-gpu-pool-3; root cause appears to be burst-policy + slow scale-down. Temporary guardrails added.
- Alert fatigue metric creeping up: paging overlap increased by 18% week-over-week — small follow-up to refine page dedup rules.
- Night shift handoffs introduced a short checklist (see Handoff checklist section) — please use and add improvements.

Incident summaries (short):
1) INC-2026-1187 — embeddings p99 spike (Dec 17 ~ 03:12–03:47 UTC)
   - Symptoms: sudden increase in p99 (from ~420ms to ~3.2s) and CPU saturation on embedding-workers-12..15. Errors: transient 500s in fronting service for 8% of requests.
   - Initial triage: alerts routed to oncall-ml, SRE joined within 6m. Canary traffic showed KV cache miss ratio jumped 40% coincident with a config rollout (cache TTL policy change) from a product PR.
   - Immediate mitigations: rolled back TTL change in config repo (PR revert #GITHUB-PR-redis-autoscale-fix), triggered cache-warm job to pre-populate hot prefixes, scaled up embedding-workers by +2 while suppressing aggressive autoscale-down policy.
   - Outcome: latency returned to baseline ~03:47 UTC. Post-incident state: metrics stable but cold-start error rate slightly elevated for ~2h.
   - Next steps: formal RCA in progress (linked). Action owners: Marco — validate preflight canaries for cache policy; Aaliyah — add a guard in config rollout pipeline to block TTL > X without canary percentage.

2) Autoscaler thrash — dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (Dec 15 22:00–23:30 UTC)
   - Symptoms: rapid add/remove cycles of GPU nodes (5 adds, 4 removes), increased evictions of short-lived pods, queue latency increased for short-burst jobs.
   - Probable cause: new burst-policy (enabled for a test tenant) + scale-down cooldown too short (30s). Combined with imprecise pod-resource-requests for the test workload.
   - Mitigation: increased cooldown to 3m, pinned reserved capacity for the test tenant for the next 48h, added throttling on scale-up for that pool.
   - Follow-up: Runbook update (autoscale policies) + ticket to infra team: INFRA-2026-934 (Samir).

SLO health & notes:
- Hosted inference (text-generation): overall OK. 99.9% within latency target for the week. A/B traffic to newer kernel still within expected range.
- Embeddings SLO: brief P99 breach described above. Weekly burn rate bumped to 1.4x target due to the spike — watch next week's rolling 7d.
- Dedication pool throughput: minor degradation during autoscale thrash windows, but no sustained SLO breach.
- Observability gap: we still lack token-level KV miss telemetry aggregated by model-version; opening ONB-2026-47 to track.

Runbook & operational changes (tentative):
- Add pre-deploy canary step specifically for cache/TTL related flags. (Owner: Marco)
- Add a circuit-breaker: if global KV miss rate increases > 25% in 5m, automatically revert TTL/rollout via pipeline. (Owner: Rina)
- Autoscaler policy defaults: change scale-down cooldown to 3m for dedicated pools; document per-pool overrides. (Owner: Samir)
- Alert routing: collapse duplicate pages for the same incident across embedding-service / cache-alerts if correlation > 0.8 to reduce duplicates. (Owner: Eve)

On-call handoff log (explicit entries for end-of-day -> night):
- Handoff 2026-12-19 23:00 UTC:
  - Outgoing: Marco (day) -> Incoming: Aaliyah (night)
  - Key notes: embedding incident residuals (cache warm jobs still running at low rate), autoscale cooldown increased, pinned dedicated-gpu-pool-3 for test tenant.
  - Open tasks handed over: INFRA-2026-934 (verify cooldown), ONB-2026-47 (create token-level telemetry stub), follow-up on RCAs.
  - Contact list: oncall-sre@redwood.ai, infra-pager (pagerduty: +1-555-0123), ml-oncall Slack channel #ml-oncall.

- Handoff 2026-12-20 07:00 UTC (night -> morning):
  - Outgoing: Aaliyah -> Incoming: Samir
  - Key notes: Stable overnight; small flurries of cache-warm errors (timeouts) detected ~05:12 UTC. Reduced the aggressiveness of cache-warm retries.
  - Open tasks: reproduce cache-warm timeouts in staging, increase logging verbosity for warm-job (Marco).

Daily standup snippets (selected):
- Dec 16: quick note about adding circuit-breaker thresholds to rollout pipeline — flagged as high priority.
- Dec 17: incident; SRE oncall rerouted; implemented rollback and warm job.
- Dec 18: monitoring alert tuning; reduced noise by silencing duplicate alerts from worker-heartbeat.
- Dec 19: autoscale thrash follow-up; pinned reserved capacity for impacted tenant.

Action items (short tracker):
- Marco: implement pre-deploy canary gating for cache-related flags — due 2026-12-27.
- Aaliyah: add pipeline guard that prevents TTL > 600s without 5% canary — due 2026-12-22.
- Samir: change scale-down cooldown defaults and add per-pool override docs — due 2026-12-24.
- Eve: refine alert deduping logic in PagerDuty -> SLO owner mapping; produce noise-reduction plan — due 2026-12-28.
- Rina: draft the temporary circuit-breaker script and coordinate with CI owners — due 2026-12-23.

Questions & unresolved items (notes to self / TODO):
- Why did the config rollout change (TTL flag) slip through the current preflight? Need to trace the PR review chain and CI gating. PR author assigned: @product-team.
- Are there additional tenants using burst-policy that we have not flagged? Need a quick inventory query (Samir).
- Should we temporarily widen SLO objective margin for embeddings during holiday traffic? Ops to discuss Tuesday.

Useful links referenced above:
- RCA draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-1187+RCA
- Autoscale policy runbook (work-in-progress): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Autoscale-Runbook
- PagerDuty noise dashboard: https://internal.redwood.ai/ops/pagerduty-noise

Handoff checklist (new, please use and append):
- [ ] Confirm no active pages unacknowledged
- [ ] Share immediate outstanding incidents and their mitigations
- [ ] Confirm scale/rollout changes pinned or rolled back
- [ ] Confirm any running mitigation jobs (cache-warm, draining, etc.) and owner
- [ ] List top three follow-ups and expected due dates

Notes to the next shift lead:
- If you see repeated cache warm timeouts, temporarily disable retries and file a follow-up with the job owner — warmers are expensive and risk cascading retries.
- For any autoscale thrash, pin capacity and escalate to infra-provisioning; do not rely on scale-in/out until cooldowns are validated.

Appendix (raw logs pointers):
- Embedding-workers logs (sample window): internal-s3://ops-logs/embeddings/2026-12-17/03-00-04.tar.gz
- Autoscaler events: k8s-events://dedicated-gpu-pool-3/2026-12-15-22-events

End of stitch doc. Add edits inline or append notes in the Confluence RCA. This doc is intentionally lightweight — use it as a handoff + quick status summary.
